chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three (things) are cursed. Accursed is the one who does this – The defecation in the shade of encampments (public places), and the prevention of the allocated water, and the blocking of the travelled road'.
ai.seo_question: What are the three cursed actions in Shia Islamic tradition regarding public conduct?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi identifies three specific acts of negligence—defecating in the shade of thoroughfares, withholding water from travelers, and blocking public paths—that incur a divine curse, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal rights (Haqq al-Nas). It underscores the Prophet’s teaching that public utility and cleanliness are not merely social courtesies but spiritual obligations, where obstructing others' ease is akin to a form of minor disbelief.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Three (things) are cursed. Accursed is the one who does this – The defecation in the shade of encampments (public places), and the prevention of the allocated water, and the blocking of the travelled road’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘There are three things whose performer is condemned: Defecating in recreational places, blocking allocated water and public roads.’”
